# Worked examples and the library

## Worked examples

Each is a real prompt's answer in `references/examples/<id>/` (`prompt.json` is the prompt), compiling clean. They show each asset kind and pattern once; they are not a catalogue of answers. Plan every prompt from `planning.md` and `capabilities.md`, and read the example that shows a pattern you need.

| example | what it shows |
|---|---|
| `sales-mutual-nda-web-form` | web form → workflow → library document template → sign: the simplest whole flow |
| `fin-credit-application` | Agreement Desk request + approvals, a request type two workflows share (the shared tail), approvers as user and group placeholders the README names |
| `sales-nda-salesforce-opportunity` | Salesforce start: the document filled from the record, the record updated at the end |
| `ai-risk-scoring-routing` | an AI agent in a request workflow, approvals routed on its score |
| `legal-litigation-settlement` | a NEW eSignature template (inline document, printed to PDF), ID Verification, parallel signers |
| `proc-sourcing-rfp-nda-bulk` | bulk send of an eSignature template, and a workflow started by an envelope event |
| `fin-loan-agreement-kba` | an API start that sends an eSignature template from a workflow, KBA, integration notes |
| `legal-hold-notice` | a document template uploaded on its own (bulk send), a library workflow, a schedule start |
| `legal-clm-nda-self-service` | CLM workflow + Doc Gen form (inline) and its configuration |
| `clm-eform-contract-request` | a CLM eForm whose submission starts a CLM workflow |
| `webform-volunteer-waiver-from-template` | web form only: built from an eSignature template, signed on the form |
| `legal-power-of-attorney-notary` | nothing can be built: notBuildable, and gaps with what to do instead |

## The library

The library specs the examples compile from, in `references/library/<kind>/specs/<id>.json` (eSignature templates in `scripts/assets/esign-templates/`, with their PDFs). A manifest can name any of them by id. Start from the closest one; a changed copy, or a new spec, gets an id of its own in the project (an id in both the project and the library is refused). "Proven" means a committed live verify report. The gallery repo holds more library specs the gallery repo: copy one into the project under a new id to start from it.
